title: hotfix: stabilize SLO enforcer backoff & hysteresis ordering during regional failover
author: Priya Singh
release_notes: Fix: Ensure deterministic ordering of backoff/hysteresis updates to avoid cascading load-shedding during regional failover
Stability: Prevent SLO enforcer state races that could trigger over-aggressive failover policies
Observability: Add metrics and traces to surface ordering and state transitions
description:
Context: During a production incident on 2026-02-14 we observed repeated SLO breaches in EU region during a cross-region failover (root cause: non-deterministic ordering in SLO enforcer backoff + hysteresis state updates). The enforcer would sometimes apply backoff before hysteresis stabilization completed, causing aggressive load-shedding and cascading traffic shifts to other regions. This PR makes the state update ordering deterministic, serializes in-memory enforcer mutations, and adds protective guards to avoid transient over-shedding.

What this PR does:
- Serialize SLO enforcer state updates using a per-region sequencer to guarantee ordering of backoff and hysteresis transitions.
- Introduce a short hysteresis-commit phase to delay irreversible load-shedding decisions until dependent state updates arrive.
- Add idempotency keys to remote enforcer RPCs used during regional coordination to avoid double-apply on retries.
- Tighten backoff evaluation to prefer grace periods when a failover is in-progress.
- Add comprehensive unit and integration tests that reproduce the race and assert stable behavior.
- Add new metrics/traces: slo_enforcer.update_sequence, slo_enforcer.hysteresis_commits, slo_enforcer.double_apply_count.

Why: The incident analysis (linked in Linear ENG-4321) shows a narrow race where upstream region disconnects + concurrent backoff calculation could reorder events. Making ordering explicit and observable reduces likelihood of mass load-shedding as well as makes debugging incidents straightforward.

Testing and rollout:
- Unit tests added (hysteresis_test.go) to cover ordering scenarios.
- Integration test added to perf-canary suite to simulate regional failover.
- Feature guarded behind runtime flag slo_enforcer.ordered_updates (default: true for rollout).
- Gradual rollout: start with canary (10% of traffic) -> 50% -> 100% over a 4 hour window, with automatic rollback if slo_enforcer.over_shed_rate > 0.5% over 10m.

Related: Linear ENG-4321, incident writeup: docs/incident/2026-02-15-slo-failover.md.

Notes: This is a hotfix intended for immediate deployment; changes kept minimal and focused on ordering/guards. Longer-term followups: replace in-memory sequencer with persistent ordering in Dedicated control-plane (follow-up ENG-4350).
